variants.name: Classic Handler hierarchy with successor pointer
variants.idiom_name: abstract Handler with successor pointer and virtual handle()
variants.implementation_notes: The GoF structure as written: an abstract Handler declares the request operation and holds a pointer to its successor; concrete handlers either process the request or delegate to the successor, and a terminal handler returns the default result. The standard library ships no pipeline, so the structure is hand-written; use references or smart pointers for ownership and keep the chain alive for the executor's lifetime. Choose this form when handlers are stateful objects shared across requests or the toolchain predates C++11.
pitfalls: Raw successor pointers dangle when handlers are stack objects constructed out of chain order; build the chain on the heap or fix construction order.
Forgetting the terminal handler makes every handle() return false without a diagnostic.
Virtual dispatch plus per-request handler objects add an allocation and an indirect call per hop; build the chain once, not per request.

variants.name: Callable chain with std::function / vector of handlers
variants.idiom_name: std::function<bool(Request&)> chain, or a vector of callables walked by a loop
variants.implementation_notes: Modern C++ collapses the hierarchy into callables: each handler is a `std::function<bool(Request&)>` that returns whether it consumed the request, and the chain is either a linked composition in which each callable closes over the next or a vector walked by a dispatch loop. No inheritance, no virtual dispatch, and handlers can be lambdas capturing their own state. Crow's middleware (before_handle/after_handle with response.end() stopping later middleware) is the framework form of the same idea. Prefer this variant once the toolchain is C++11 or later and handlers are small functions rather than large stateful objects.
pitfalls: std::function heap-allocates for captures above its small-buffer threshold and adds an indirect call per hop; keep captures small or use a non-owning function reference on hot paths.
Composing by value copies lambda state, including a chain that captures itself; move captures in and avoid accidental recursion through the chain.
An exception thrown out of a handler leaves the remaining links unrun; decide whether exceptions stop the chain or belong to each handler's contract.
